The Origins of the Cold War, 1941–58

Grand Alliance, Wartime Conferences, Containment, Berlin Crisis, NATO & Hungary 1956
Audio • Quiz Hub
US Air Force Official Photographer (1948–1949) US National Archives (NARA)
Cover Source Study 1948–1949
Operation Vittles — C-54 Skymaster Approaching Tempelhof, West Berlin
During Stalin’s eleven-month blockade of West Berlin (June 1948 – May 1949), Allied aircraft flew over 275,000 flights along three narrow air corridors to sustain two million civilians without firing a shot.
3 Details to Spot in This Photograph:
1. Four-engine US Air Force C-54 ("TROOP CARRIER") with landing gear lowered over ruined Berlin apartments.
2. Crowds of West Berlin children standing atop post-war rubble mounds cheering incoming food and coal supplies.
3. Showed how Truman upheld containment peacefully without firing on Soviet forces.
Class Discussion: Why was Stalin unwilling to order Soviet fighter planes to shoot down unarmed Western cargo aircraft over East Germany?
Q1 • Two Consequences 8m (2×4m)
Two separate 4-mark consequences. State each consequence, give a specific date/fact, and explain what it led to (10 mins).
Q2 • Narrative Account 8 Marks
3 chronological paragraphs (Beginning → Key Developments → Outcome) linked by causal phrases + own knowledge (12 mins).
Q3 • Explain Importance 16m (2×8m)
Answer 2 of 3 choices. For each 8-mark choice, write two paragraphs explaining why X was important for Y (25 mins).
Pearson Edexcel (1HI0) Topic Checklist • Key Topic 1 Taught Revised
1.1 • Early tension between East and West
The Grand Alliance; outcomes of the Tehran, Yalta & Potsdam conferences
Ideological differences between the superpowers & the attitudes of Stalin, Truman & Churchill
Impact on US-Soviet relations of the development of the atomic bomb, the Long & Novikov telegrams & the creation of Soviet satellite states in Eastern Europe
1.2 • The development of the Cold War
Impact on US-Soviet relations of the Truman Doctrine & the Marshall Plan, 1947
Significance: Cominform (1947), Comecon (1949) & the formation of NATO (1949)
Berlin: its division into zones; The Berlin Crisis (blockade & airlift) of 1948-49 & its impact; formation of the Federal Republic of Germany & German Democratic Republic
1.3 • The Cold War intensifies
Significance: arms race; formation of the Warsaw Pact
Events in 1956 leading to the Hungarian Uprising & Khrushchev’s response
International reaction to the Soviet invasion of Hungary

Cold War Crises, 1958–70

Berlin Ultimatum & Wall, Cuban Missile Crisis, Nuclear Treaties & Czechoslovakia 1968
Audio • Quiz Hub
Archival Press Photographer (October 1961) Wikimedia Commons / Cold War Berlin Archive
Cover Source Study October 1961
Tank Standoff Across Friedrichstrasse at Checkpoint Charlie, Berlin
Two months after East German troops sealed the border on 13 August 1961, US and Soviet tanks stood engines running just 100 metres apart at Checkpoint Charlie—symbolising the razor-thin margin between stalemate and nuclear war.
3 Details to Spot in This Photograph:
1. Soviet battle tanks positioned directly behind stacked concrete barrier beams blocking Friedrichstrasse.
2. Berlin U-Bahn ("U") station sign and clock overhead showing an everyday city sliced in two.
3. Tank commanders in padded helmets peering from open turret hatches during the tense 16-hour standoff.
Class Discussion: Why did building the Berlin Wall simultaneously ease the risk of war over Berlin while handing the West a propaganda victory?
Q1 • Two Consequences 8m (2×4m)
Two separate 4-mark consequences. State each consequence, give a specific date/fact, and explain what it led to (10 mins).
Q2 • Narrative Account 8 Marks
3 chronological paragraphs (Beginning → Key Developments → Outcome) linked by causal phrases + own knowledge (12 mins).
Q3 • Explain Importance 16m (2×8m)
Answer 2 of 3 choices. For each 8-mark choice, write two paragraphs explaining why X was important for Y (25 mins).
Pearson Edexcel (1HI0) Topic Checklist • Key Topic 2 Taught Revised
2.1 • Increased tension between East and West
Refugee problem in Berlin, Khrushchev’s Berlin ultimatum (1958) & the summit meetings of 1959–61
Impact of the Cuban Revolution on relations with the USA & the Soviet Union (incl. the refusal of the USA to recognise Castro’s government & the closer relations with the Soviet Union); Bay of Pigs incident
Opposition in Czechoslovakia to Soviet control: the Prague Spring
2.2 • Cold War crises
Construction of the Berlin Wall, 1961
Events of the Cuban Missile Crisis
The Brezhnev Doctrine & the re-establishment of Soviet control in Czechoslovakia
2.3 • Reaction to crisis
Impact of the construction of the Berlin Wall on US-Soviet relations; Kennedy’s visit to West Berlin in 1963
Consequences of the Cuban Missile Crisis (incl. the ‘hotline’); Attempts at arms control: the Limited Test Ban Treaty (1963); the Outer Space Treaty (1967); & the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (1968)
International reaction to Soviet measures in Czechoslovakia

The End of the Cold War, 1970–91

Détente, Afghanistan, Olympic Boycotts, Reagan’s SDI, Gorbachev & Collapse of the USSR
Audio • Quiz Hub
Lear 21 (Wikimedia Commons) (November 1989) Wikimedia Commons Historical Archive
Cover Source Study November 1989
Citizens Atop the Berlin Wall Before the Brandenburg Gate
Following Mikhail Gorbachev’s repudiation of the Brezhnev Doctrine and East Germany’s sudden border opening on 9 November 1989, crowds climbed freely onto the Berlin Wall in front of the Brandenburg Gate without a single Soviet tank intervening.
3 Details to Spot in This Photograph:
1. Hundreds of East and West Berliners standing shoulder-to-shoulder atop the rounded cap of the Berlin Wall.
2. The Brandenburg Gate and tall border floodlight tower rising directly behind the celebrating crowd.
3. Hand-painted "LOVE & PEACE IN WEST & EAST" banners taped across the graffiti-covered western wall face.
Class Discussion: Did the Cold War end primarily because of Ronald Reagan’s military pressure or Mikhail Gorbachev’s internal reforms?
Q1 • Two Consequences 8m (2×4m)
Two separate 4-mark consequences. State each consequence, give a specific date/fact, and explain what it led to (10 mins).
Q2 • Narrative Account 8 Marks
3 chronological paragraphs (Beginning → Key Developments → Outcome) linked by causal phrases + own knowledge (12 mins).
Q3 • Explain Importance 16m (2×8m)
Answer 2 of 3 choices. For each 8-mark choice, write two paragraphs explaining why X was important for Y (25 mins).

TASK A • Number Events A–H in Chronological Order (1 = Earliest, 8 = Latest) & Write the Month/Year [8 Marks]
ID Key Topic 3 Specification Event (1972–91) Month / Year Order
A Mikhail Gorbachev resigns on Christmas Day, formally dissolving the Soviet Union
B Nixon and Brezhnev sign the SALT 1 ABM and Interim Missile Agreements in Moscow
C Soviet troops invade Afghanistan to overthrow Hafizullah Amin and install Babrak Karmal
D Ronald Reagan announces the space-based Strategic Defence Initiative (SDI / "Star Wars")
E 35 nations sign the Helsinki Accords covering Borders, Cooperation, and Human Rights
F East Berliners surge through checkpoints after Schabowski’s broadcast, toppling the Berlin Wall
G Reagan and Gorbachev sign the INF Treaty eliminating intermediate-range nuclear missiles
H The USA leads over 60 nations in boycotting the Moscow Summer Olympic Games

1. Soviet Red Army invades Afghanistan (December 1979)

Explain how this transformed Communist rule in Poland, Hungary, and East Germany in 1989:

Explain how Boris Yeltsin’s victory led directly to the end of the USSR in December 1991:
